case_studies.title: Continual Knowledge Updating in LLM Systems: Learning Through Multi-Timescale Memory Dynamics
case_studies.abstract: LLMs are trained once, then deployed into a world that never stops changing. External memory compensates for this, but most systems manage it explicitly rather than letting it adapt on its own. Biological memory works differently: coupled multi-timescale dynamics make new associations immediately usable, strengthen what repetition confirms, and let the rest fade. We argue that external memory should follow a similar principle. In Memini, this view takes the form of an associative memory that organizes knowledge as a directed graph. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of outdated knowledge in large language models by building a system called Memini that uses a unique memory dynamics approach, resulting in more adaptable and accurate knowledge updates. The system uses a directed graph to organize knowledge and allows for immediate adaptation to new information. This research may improve the performance of language models in various applications.

case_studies.title: Look Once, Beam Twice: Camera-Primed Real-Time Double-Directional mmWave Beam Management for Vehicular Connectivity
case_studies.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequencies promise multi-gigabit connectivity for vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks, but face challenges in terms of severe path loss and mobility-related beam misalignment. Reliable V2X connectivity requires fast, double-directional beam alignment. However, existing methods suffer from high training overhead and limited generalization to unseen scenarios. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of beam misalignment in vehicle-to-everything networks by building a hybrid model-based system that uses camera sensing for real-time double-directional mmWave beam management, resulting in faster and more reliable connectivity. The system, called VIBE, combines machine learning with traditional beamforming methods. This technology has the potential to improve vehicular connectivity in mmWave frequencies.

case_studies.title: Automatically Finding and Validating Unexpected Side-Effects of Interventions on Language Models
case_studies.abstract: We present an automated, contrastive evaluation pipeline for auditing the behavioral impact of interventions on large language models. Given a base model $M_1$ and an intervention model $M_2$, our method compares their free-form, multi-token generations across aligned prompt contexts and produces human-readable, statistically validated natural-language hypotheses describing how the models differ, along with recurring themes that summarize patterns across validated hypotheses. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of identifying unexpected side-effects of changes to language models, by building an automated evaluation pipeline that compares the behavior of two models, the result is a set of human-readable hypotheses describing the differences. The pipeline can identify recurring themes and patterns in the differences. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: Order Matters: Improving Domain Adaptation by Reordering Data
case_studies.abstract: Domain shift remains a key challenge in deploying machine learning models to the real world. Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to address this by minimising domain discrepancy during training, but the discrepancy estimates suffer from high variance in stochastic settings, which can stifle the theoretical benefits of the method. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of high variance in domain adaptation for machine learning models by building a new technique called ORDERED, which reduces discrepancy estimation error by optimising the order of training data. The result is a more accurate and reliable domain adaptation method. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.
